r1-A.notes: pass 1: Reply timer cleared on puzzle open (src/main.ts, diff.patch:1060); accepts any move that still forces mate via defenderLost search (src/chess.ts, diff.patch:668), the most correct puzzle judging. e2e solves every puzzle and drags with a finger. The search adds complexity but is contained. Visual polished: status bar, move list, puzzle grid, solved modal naming the move. | pass 2: No real bugs found. Accepts any move that still forces mate (B/diff.patch:1112), cancels the reply timer (B/diff.patch:1060), uses pointer capture, and has a real touch-drag e2e test. Very polished UI: move list, puzzle grid with solved ticks, modal results with View board. main.ts at 673 lines is large but readable. | pass 3: No bugs found. Puzzle accepts any move that still forces mate (forcesMate/defenderLost), the smartest puzzle logic here; cancelReply on every mode change, pending reply flushed on pointerdown. SAN move list, keyboard, overlays with View board. Only 27 unit tests (one per rule) keeps code_quality below F. Wins over F on correctness of puzzle handling.

r1-B.notes: pass 1: Solid compact engine; all rules tested. Real bug: defender reply is a bare setTimeout never cleared (src/main.ts, diff.patch:563-573); switching puzzle within 550 ms runs step++ and a reply on the new puzzle, corrupting it. Tapping the selected piece reselects instead of deselecting. render() rebuilds innerHTML each time. Visual: clean modals, but desktop left-aligned and sparse, tiny coordinates, select-only picker. | pass 2: Bug: the reply setTimeout (F/diff.patch:567) is never cleared on puzzle change. Checking an alternative mate replays the whole line from the puzzle FEN (F/diff.patch:538) instead of using the current game. The phone header layout differs between modes, Puzzle solved shows three times, the knight and king glyphs look rough, and puzzles are chosen from a dropdown. | pass 3: Minor race: reply setTimeout at main.ts:150-159 not cleared; switching within 550 ms runs step++ on the new puzzle, marking a mate-in-1 solved with no move (sub-second). Puzzles tab always reopens puzzle 1 (main.ts:349). Game.play has no legality check; relies on callers. 35 unit, 5 e2e. Phone header layout shifts between modes. Below X on code_quality for thinner e2e.

r1-C.notes: pass 1: Correct puzzle flow: replyTimer is cleared on startPlay/openPuzzle, alternative final mate accepted, selection limited to the player side. e2e solves every puzzle; insufficient material includes same-colour bishops (unasked). Code weaker: render() rebuilds the whole app innerHTML including tabs on every render (src/main.ts). Visual is plain: result card in side panel, desktop slightly left-aligned, select plus buttons. | pass 2: No real bugs found. The reply timer is cleared on navigation (Z/diff.patch:529). The e2e test solves all 12 puzzles and covers castling and en passant via the UI. A wrong move is flagged by a message only, with no square highlight (Z/diff.patch:590). Clean, consistent UI in both themes with a solid promotion dialog, but the desktop layout is sparse and there is no move list. | pass 3: No bugs found. Game class with insufficient material; replyTimer cleared in startPlay and openPuzzle. Strong targeted tests (castling through check, b1-only attack, 100th half-move mate) and 8 e2e, but only 27 unit. Visual clean but desktop layout hugs the left with half the viewport empty. Below A on code_quality: fewer unit tests.

Polished branded UI with an amber accent, move list, puzzle grid and game-over modal. A wrong move is shown, then taken back after 700 ms. | pass 3: No bugs found. Modular engine, 69 unit tests, but only 4 e2e (fewest). Wrong move flashed and undone after 700 ms; clearTimers on new game and puzzle open; any mating move accepted. New game restarts from ?fen start, acceptable. Polished amber theme with overlays and move list. Below E on code_quality due to thin e2e.

r1-E.notes: pass 1: Same stale-timer bug as A: reply window.setTimeout (src/main.ts, diff.patch:655-660) is not stored; resetTransient only clears wrongTimer, so switching puzzle mid-reply corrupts the new puzzle. No unit test that check is detected (describe 'check, mate, stalemate' at diff.patch:1351 tests only mate, stalemate, undo). Visual: promotion picker without title or cancel, duplicate status line and two New game buttons on game over. | pass 2: Rules are correct and well tested (43). Bug: the reply setTimeout (D/diff.patch:655) is not tracked or cleared by resetTransient (D/diff.patch:587), so changing puzzle during the 450 ms delay plays the old reply on the new puzzle. UI is decent with a puzzle grid, but the promotion picker has no label and New game is duplicated in the mate state. | pass 3: Real bug: startGame (main.ts:36-49) never resets solved (only startPuzzle does, main.ts:57); canInteract (main.ts:82) requires !solved, so after solving any puzzle the Two players board and New game are locked. Normal users hit this, breaking pass-and-play. Also uncleared reply timer at main.ts:130. Visual: checkmate text shown three times, duplicated New game.

r2-A.notes: pass 1: Defender reply played synchronously with an animation delay (src/main.ts, diff.patch:1000-1015), so no timer race; wrong move undone and flashed, wrongTimer cleared. 53 unit tests plus 15 e2e including CDP touch tap/drag, threefold and castling via UI. Most polished UI: blurred modals, move list, puzzle grid with solved ticks, hint, promotion cancel; good at both widths and themes. | pass 2: No real bugs found. The defender reply is applied synchronously and animated (C/diff.patch:1010), so there is no timer race. Broadest tests: 53 unit (extra perft positions, puzzle validation) and 15 e2e incl. touch tap/drag, castling and threefold via the UI. Most polished UI: overlays, move list, puzzle grid, hint. CSS is heavy (648 lines). | pass 3: No bugs found. Position class with make/unmake and legal-move cache; defender reply is immediate so no timer race. 53 unit and 15 e2e tests, the strongest suite. Polished blurred-backdrop overlays, puzzle grid, Hint. Scored 9 on correctness only because its puzzle checking is less forgiving than D's forced-mate acceptance; very close runner-up.

r2-B.notes: pass 1: Clear engine and thorough rule tests (36). Clean but plain UI with a sparse desktop sidebar. | pass 3: Rules correct. Minor race: reply setTimeout at main.ts:138 never cancelled; Restart/Next/mode switch within 450 ms runs state.step += 1 on the new puzzle (sub-second, rare). No research note. Visual plainest of the set: bare panel, redundant checkmate text, small desktop promotion picker. Ranks below X/Z on visual and polish.

Minor race: async wait(450) reply at main.ts:134-146 never cancelled; switching puzzle within 450 ms runs solIdx++ and can mark the new puzzle solved (sub-second, rare). 21 unit, 6 e2e incl. retry and stalemate. Neat overlays both themes. Beats Z on code_quality: more thorough e2e.
